html:
Ecuador is a country on the Pacific coast of South America, crossed by the equator that gives it its name. It has been a separate republic since 1830.

Quito was the northern capital of the Inca Empire, and Atahualpa had his power base here when he won the Inca civil war, just before the Spanish arrived. Under Spain the region was ruled from Quito as an audiencia, first under Peru and then under the Viceroyalty of New Granada. Independence was won at the Battle of Pichincha in 1822 by Antonio José de Sucre, and the land joined Gran Colombia until 1830.

The young country swung between the Catholic conservatives of the highlands and the liberal merchants of the port of Guayaquil:

  • Gabriel García Moreno ruled in the 1860s and 1870s as a strict Catholic reformer.
  • Eloy Alfaro led the Liberal Revolution of 1895, separating church and state.
  • Cocoa exports boomed around 1900; from the 1950s Ecuador was the world's largest exporter of bananas.

A border war with Peru in 1941 cost Ecuador much of its claimed Amazon land; a final peace came only in 1998. Oil from the Amazon became the main export from the 1970s, and in 2000 the country gave up its own currency for the US dollar. Its Galápagos Islands, where Darwin studied finches and tortoises in 1835, are among the world's great nature reserves.
sum: Ecuador is a country on the Pacific coast of South America, crossed by the equator that gives it its name. It has been a separate republic since 1830.
